messages:
sanjay: quick heads up — saw a perf regression in mixed-quant serving during long-prefix perf runs. FP8 path OK, but the int4 path is producing NaNs/Inf after ~4k tokens when KV cache grows. attaching profiler snippet in a reply.
lee: ugh. is this reproducible locally or only on dedicated clusters?
maria: reproduced on my laptop with the same workload (long chat history + long generation). seems correlated with the kernel selector choosing the int4 GEMM for attention when seq_len > 2048 and kv_size high.
kevin: interesting — selector chooses int4 because latency estimate lower, but it doesn't account for dynamic scale blowup from repeated prefix rescaling. profiling shows dot-prod peaks and then sudden NaN spike.
perf-bot: [automated profile] profile_id=pf_2026_03_15_09; top hotspots: attention_int4_gemm, kv_read_rescale, softmax_fp_conv
sanjay: paste of quick trace:
```
# short excerpt from perf log
t=0.123 ms kernel=fp8_attention
t=0.130 ms kernel=int4_attention  <-- chosen
... seq grow to 4096
t=0.403 ms kernel=int4_attention  <-- NaN detected in output
```
olivia: can we add a cheap numeric-safety check in the selector? e.g., if kv_entries > X and prefix_ratio > Y, prefer fp8 or int8 fallback.
lee: yes — propose heuristic: bucket kv_size into small/med/large, if large force conservative kernel or enable pre-rescale.
maria: also suggest smoothquant-like pre-scale on query/key weights at load time per-layer to avoid per-step rescale drift. cheap ops and helps int4 stability.
kevin: implementation plan:
- selector change: add kv_bucket feature and simple threshold rule
- runtime: insert a tiny "validate_output" CUDA kernel that checks for NaN/Inf on first N tokens of generation and triggers fallback if seen
- config: expose "numeric_safety.mode" with options [off, warn, fallback]
sanjay: prototype patch incoming. one caveat: validation kernel adds ~0.2ms per chunk. but prevents full-job failures so worth it for dedicated SLA customers.
olivia: also add logging metric "numeric_fallback_count" and alert when >0.1% of requests.
kevin: test plan: microbench with seqs 512/2048/4096, run mixed-quant kernels with/without pre-scale, compare latency and failure rates. I'll open a PR with benchmarks.
perf-bot: action created: PERF-764 add selector kv_bucket heuristic -> assignee kevin, due 2026-03-22
lee: ack. if anyone runs into false positives from the validator, please ping me and attach the mini-repro script.
maria: mini repro in case helpful:
```
python -m repro.long_prefix --model redwood-small-4bit --prefix-len 4096 --gen-len 512 --quant=int4
```
sanjay: thanks team. priority: prevent customer-visible NaNs, then tune latency. :thumbsup:
